safetyNote: Deadly poisonous: Lepiota brunneoincarnata contains amatoxins that can cause delayed gastrointestinal illness followed by severe liver injury. Do not eat or taste it. If ingestion is suspected, contact an emergency service or poison centre immediately, even before symptoms appear.

sections.title: Deadly dapperling
sections.text: Lepiota brunneoincarnata is a small pinkish-brown dapperling. Its cap is initially hemispherical, then convex to nearly flat, often with a low central umbo. The 2.5–6 cm cap has a darker brown to purplish-brown centre; towards the margin its surface breaks into small brown-pink scales over a paler cream or flesh-coloured background. Cap scales and colour vary among specimens.

sections.title: Gills, stem and ring
sections.text: The crowded gills are free from the stem and whitish to cream; the spore print is white. The narrow stem is roughly 2.5–5.5 cm long, paler and smoother above, with brown-pink fibrous scales on its lower part. A small upper ring or ring zone is fragile and may disappear. Cap flesh remains white, while stem flesh or its base can flush pinkish to wine-red when damaged; reddening is variable and must not be used alone for identification.

sections.title: Habitat and lookalikes
sections.text: It occurs in broadleaf woods, parks, gardens, lawns, path edges and other grassy places, usually in summer or autumn in Europe. Small lepiotas resemble one another, and this species can grow near edible grassland mushrooms. Cap size, a faint ring, or the absence of visible reddening cannot establish that a collection is safe.

sections.title: Amatoxin poisoning
sections.text: This species can cause the phalloid syndrome. After a symptom-free interval, often about 6–24 hours, severe vomiting and diarrhoea may begin; serious liver injury can follow, sometimes with kidney injury. Published cases show severe poisoning from amounts well below 100 g, so no reassuring quantity threshold should be inferred. Suspected ingestion is a medical emergency even if the person currently feels well.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The white-background plate shows a whole mushroom, a longitudinal section, a cap surface view and the free-gilled underside. These views highlight the dark scaly cap centre, the fragile ring zone, the lower-stem scales and the slight pink flush at the cut stem.
